What crosses at the hook floor is the admission verdict, and the hook-facing rows carry that tie-back; this row states the scanner's INPUT to that floor, which is machinery behind the crossing rather than the crossing.

Whether a vendored-source upstream is a party the frame should carry is a live question for the frame's owner; until it is answered this row must not manufacture a tie-back to a crossing that describes something else.

docs/declared-absences.rationale: The seam exists because a second reader needs the same facts: tests/test_dogfood_sync.py loads the file as its SCAFFOLD_OMISSIONS declaration, so the file - not an import - is the shared home, which keeps the stdlib-only kit script free of any dependency on a test module.

project-trajectory/hooks/pre-commit.contract: git invokes this hook at commit time with no arguments; exit 0 admits the staged write into governed state, any nonzero exit refuses the commit, and the failing check is named on stderr. `git commit --no-verify` skips the invocation entirely, so this seam admits only the writes a session routes through it.
project-trajectory/hooks/pre-commit.notes: The FACING row for the hook floor, and it is deliberately separate from the rows that model the floor's COMPOSITION. Those state which script the hook runs - an internal call between two in-tree endpoints - while the crossing is the contract git holds the hook to: git invokes, the exit code admits or refuses. A tie-back on an internal-call row would claim a realization that row's own contract does not state, so the gap was never a missing surface but a missing FACING. The bypass rides the contract rather than hiding behind it: what discharges `no unchecked write enters governed state` is this seam PAIRED with a re-run of the same bar away from the bypass, never this seam alone.

project-trajectory/hooks/pre-push.contract: git invokes this hook before a push with the remote name and URL on argv and the outgoing ref pairs on stdin; exit 0 releases the push and any nonzero exit refuses it, naming the offending range on stderr. `git push --no-verify` skips the invocation, so the refusal binds only a session that routes through it.
project-trajectory/hooks/pre-push.notes: Ties back to the VERDICT crossing only, and the asymmetry with the commit-side hook is recorded rather than smoothed away. SR-020 carries both the write-in and the verdict-out crossing, but what this hook gates is content LEAVING the machine, while the write-in crossing describes the one write path INTO governed state; claiming it here would widen that crossing by assertion instead of by a frame decision. If the frame intends its write-in crossing to cover the whole git hook floor in both directions, the crossing's own text is what needs widening, not this row's attribution.
